chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About a man who says, 'Exchange my horse for your horse, and I will add to you [more value].' He (the Imam) said, 'That is not valid, but he should say, 'Give me your horse for such and such [amount], and I will give you my horse for such and such [amount].''

key_terms.أَزِيدَكَ: I will add to you (more value/money)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to phrase a barter deal involving adding value to one of the exchanged items?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the vague phrasing of 'exchange for yours with addition' (Mu'awada) lacks the necessary precision for a valid contract, requiring explicit specification of the added value to avoid Gharar (ambiguity). This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on clear terms in barter transactions to prevent disputes, distinguishing it from simple sale by ensuring both the principal items and the supplementary consideration are clearly defined. The requirement for explicit valuation reflects the broader principle of transparency in commercial dealings to ensure mutual consent.
